RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: Not estimable from the information provided

An all-woman panel is not, by itself, evidence of sex discrimination. Neither the appointee’s abbreviated biography nor your stronger academic credentials establishes who best met the job’s full criteria. Leadership and consultation experience may have carried substantial weight.

Follow up on your unanswered request. Ask for the selection criteria, their weighting, your assessment and the reasons for the appointment, subject to applicable disclosure rules.

Raise a discrimination concern if concrete evidence emerges—for example, sex-related remarks, inconsistent treatment or departures from selection rules—not simply the panel’s composition. Check local complaint deadlines now; waiting for a response may not extend them. A numerical probability would be invented.
